messages:
ana_cs: FYI customer reported a sudden change in generated product descriptions after yesterday's rollout. internal evals (regression-suite v42) passed, but customer's prompts now truncate details and add wrong pricing. ticket: https://zendesk.internal/RED-5123

customer_james: attaching the exact prompt & outputs here so you can repro. We saw behavior change at ~2026-04-20 18:10 UTC after the canary finished. prompt below + two outputs (before/after).

customer_james: Prompt:

```\nYou are ProductWriter. Create a concise product description (3 sentences) for the following item. Include features and a single sentence on pricing.
Product: AcmeFlow Pro 2.0, a workflow automator for SMBs.\n```

customer_james: Output (expected / before):
"""
AcmeFlow Pro 2.0 is a workflow automation tool designed for small and medium businesses. It features visual flow building, role-based access control, and 3rd-party integrations with Slack and Salesforce. Pricing starts at $19/user/month.\n"""

customer_james: Output (observed / after rollout):
"""
AcmeFlow Pro 2.0 is a workflow tool with integrations. Contact sales for pricing.
"""

ana_cs: Thanks — that matches the ticket. I already asked for the model id and exact request payload; customer says they were using model `redwood-instruct-1.3.0` via our hosted API and didn't set temperature (default). They also included conversation history with a short system message.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout complete: redwood-instruct-1.3.0 -> served 100% traffic at 2026-04-20T18:03:22Z (rollout-id: r-2026-04-20-1800).

mike_runtime: tagging in. Can you paste the raw curl you used? also confirm whether the customer used streaming or non-streaming. Streaming can mask partial truncation.

jordan_support: paste of customer curl (sanitized):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-1.3.0","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are ProductWriter."},{"role":"user","content":"<prompt above>"}],"max_tokens":120}'
```

jordan_support: they used non-streaming. We tried pinning to redwood-instruct-1.2.8 for them and the output returned to expected behavior (from customer's side).

mike_runtime: interesting — that suggests a behavioral change between 1.2.8 and 1.3.0. But our regression-suite v42 runs synthetic prompts and didn't flag this. Could be a prompt distribution mismatch or a tokenization/context edge case. Two immediate suspects: the new kernel's prefix pruning or a subtle change in default stop sequences.

sophia_research: I'll run targeted diffs. Can you share: (1) exact JSON payload (we need role array and whitespace preserved), (2) the tokenized ids for both versions, (3) whether the customer had a long conversation history that might push system message out of cache.

customer_james: they attached the full payload in the ticket. conversation history is only 2 messages (system + user). tokenized length ~45 tokens. No streaming.

mike_runtime: ok I'm going to try a local repro. Please run this from a machine with CUDA kernels matching prod (nvcc 12.x) because some numeric changes only show up there. Repro curl (engineers):

```
# compare outputs on 1.2.8 vs 1.3.0
for m in redwood-instruct-1.2.8 redwood-instruct-1.3.0; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.internal.redwood/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":\"You are ProductWriter.\"},{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Create a concise product description...\"}],\"max_tokens\":120}" | jq -r .choices[0].text
  echo "\n---\n"
done
```

mike_runtime: early note — when I run 1.3.0 locally with our debug log flags I see an extra token drop at generation step ~22 when the system message appears short; looks like a prefix cache eviction bug that affects small system messages. Not sure yet if it's a model behavior or runtime bug.

sophia_research: if it's runtime-level, we'd expect model behavior to differ only under certain memory/sequence patterns. I'm adding a small fuzz test: replicate with system message length 10..200 tokens and see when output changes. Also check quantization profile differences (1.3.0 used a new int8 kernel on a subset of hardware).

jordan_support: customer tried turning off system message and then 1.3.0 produced the longer output (so system message presence matters). They prefer not to change prompts.

mike_runtime: plan: (1) reproduce locally with same payload, kernel flags and a-production-kernel container; (2) bisect the runtime change that landed in the 1.3.0 rollout (PRs r3456, r3462 around kernel selection); (3) add failing prompt to regression-suite; (4) temporary mitigation — route this customer's traffic to 1.2.8 or pin them to a stable variant until fixed.

sophia_research: I'll take (3) and run a targeted eval on a batch of 20 customer prompts. If internal evals fail to catch this class we'll extend the suite to include system-message-length variants and add a tokenization check.

ana_cs: next steps for CS: I've told the customer we'll pin them to 1.2.8 while eng investigates. Assigned ticket to @mike_runtime and @sophia_research. ETA: preliminary findings in 24h. Customer expects a regression hotfix or rollback.

mike_runtime: assigned — start with reproducer, will post logs here. If we confirm runtime bug, we'll cut a hotfix for kernel selection and roll out canary ASAP.

sophia_research: posting early result: fuzzing shows divergence when system message <= 12 tokens and total context between 40-70 tokens on int8 kernel. Adding tests now.

jordan_support: customer acknowledged pin + thanks. keeping ticket open.

ana_cs: thanks everyone. please add any short debug outputs or repro notes here so we have a single source of truth. :thumbsup:
